title: Three Times My Test Failed and the LLM Was Right
why_read: A concrete, well-told anecdote about LLM-based test oracles being right when the human-written test was wrong raises a genuinely interesting point about testing AI agent behavior.
analysis: The author describes building security detectors for AI agents and finding that in several cases, the test itself encoded a wrong assumption while the LLM's judgment about agent behavior was actually correct. This is a useful, concrete illustration of a real problem in testing AI systems: when the system under test has broader contextual knowledge than the test's author, a 'test failure' may reveal a flawed test rather than a flawed system. It's a practical lesson applicable to anyone building automated evaluation or detection systems around LLM agents, grounded in specific examples rather than abstract claims.
